title: SLO attribution pipeline and latency-tiling dashboard for multi-region failover
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an end-to-end attribution pipeline that maps SLO violations to the most likely causal vectors (region, AZ, model-variant, admission policy, shard) and surface those signals in a compact latency-tiling heatmap dashboard sliced at token granularity. Goals: 1) Reduce MTTI for multi-region failover by giving SREs deterministic attribution for SLO breaches on a per-route basis. 2) Expose token-level latency patterns (prefix vs. streaming tail) to tune admission and KV-cache policies. 3) Hook the pipeline into rollout/canary flows so new model variants or quantization changes can be rapidly evaluated against regional SLOs and adaptive circuit policies. Scope: instrumentation spec, metrics ingestion & aggregation rules, dashboard UX, alerting thresholds, and a rollout plan for canary-enabled dashboards in prod. Not in scope: automated rollback orchestration (follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Metric layer emits canonical labels: environment, region, AZ, route_id, model_variant, shard_id, admission_tier, token_index_bucket, request_id
A2: New derived SLI 'regional_token_p99_latency' computed and stored with 7d retention and 1m rollups
A3: Heatmap dashboard shows token-latency tiles per route and allows pivoting by model_variant and admission_tier
A4: Pager runbook stub and an automated SLO-attribution summary report (email/Slack) for incidents rolling forward
A5: Canary traffic (5% of traffic for 24h) wired to the dashboard and no false-positive alerts during canary
implementation_notes: We will instrument at two points: (1) pre-admit (latency from ingress -> admit decision) and (2) token emission path (per-token emission timestamps). Both will carry the canonical labels.
Token-index bucketing: store token_index_bucket as string buckets: 0-7,8-31,32-127,128+ to keep cardinality bounded in metrics backend.
Aggregation: compute p50/p90/p95/p99 per (route, region, model_variant, token_index_bucket) at 1m granularity. Downsample to 5m for long-term view.
Sampling: for high-volume routes, enable deterministic sampling by trace_id hash to keep sampling stable across retries and reduce noise in attribution.
KV-cache and admission labels are critical for distinguishing load-shedding vs. model slowdown. Add admission_tier enum: normal, throttled, shed_early, degraded_fallback.
Circuit breaker linkages: include circuit_state label in metrics so dashboards can correlate p99 spikes with circuit open/close events.
Storage: use metrics namespace 'infra.sli.token_latency' and a derived aggregate 'infra.sli.regional_token_p99'.
dashboards: Initial: 'Regional Token-Latency Tiling' Grafana panel with heatmap grid: rows=routes, cols=token_index_bucket, color=p99 latency. Filters: region, model_variant, admission_tier.
Secondary: 'SLO Attribution Summary' with top-5 contributing factors to SLO loss (region/AZ/shard/model/admission) and links to traces and admission logs.
Canary view: overlay canary vs baseline latency lines and a diff heatmap to surface regressions quickly.
alerts_and_playbooks: Create composite alert: regional_token_p99 > 2x baseline AND token-tiling shows >50% of tokens in 128+ bucket > 500ms => page SRE team.
Playbook: step-by-step to run SLO-attribution job, validate metrics labels, identify top-of-stack factor, and trigger rollback or regional reroute.
Automated summary: SLO-attribution job posts top-3 suspected causes to #sre-ops with links to dashboard and PRs.
risks_and_mitigations: High-cardinality risk: mitigate by bucketing token_index and limiting label enums; run an initial dry-run to measure cardinality impact.
Metric ingestion cost: prototype with 24h retention and sample heavy routes before enabling full retention; use downsampling for 7d+.
Data consistency between regions: ensure clock sync and standardized ingest pipeline to avoid attribution mismatches; add synthetic cross-region checks.
